technical_sources.supports: The product constitution defines the bridge mission and application non-ownership boundaries.
The receiver inventory is capability-based rather than a local serial or port allowlist.
Profile compilation preserves independent receiver and child identities.
Source-derived support rejects device-specific runtime branches.
Served protocol versions five and seven remain explicit compatibility surfaces, and retired versions stay recorded.
Kernel operations and versions remain canonical and fixed-width.
Wire compatibility and semantic validation are covered by generated and golden tests.
The public kernel boundary remains bounded and versioned.
Protected bridge behavior and known evidence limits are explicit release inputs.
Service, socket, and bounded runtime relationships are canonical.
Restoration planning and stale-authority suppression are deterministic.
Receiver generations are enforced as atomic bridge authority epochs.
Stock application ownership and connector boundaries are canonical.
Core and Full preserve the two-package application-optional boundary.
The OpenRazer adaptation remains pinned to reviewed upstream source.
Stock OpenRazer and Polychromatic compatibility is qualified without a replacement application.
OpenRGB integration is exercised as a packaged plugin against stock application interfaces.
Failure certainty, route ownership, and write boundaries remain explicit.
Runtime and package performance claims use recorded limits rather than impressions.
Native transport parity uses bounded, source-validated evidence contracts.
Release qualification keeps software, application, and physical claims separate.
The final package contract is lean Core plus integration-complete Full.
Quality, dependency, security, and performance outcomes remain bounded and reviewable.
Public documentation has explicit ownership and canonical sources.
Package staging and manifests preserve component ownership and reproducibility.
Quality and performance claims are validated against canonical evidence.
